text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Russia and NATO signed an agreement in Paris on Tuesday and declared that the Cold War had officially ended.
- The presidents of Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, Ukraine and Poland dissapointed the sensation hunters in Tallinn on Tuesday after they evaluated the agreement between Russia and NATO positively.
- The renowned musician and conductor Mstislav Rostropovich will conduct the ballet Romeo and Juliet in the Vilnius opera and ballet theatre tonight.
- Lithuania's foreign trade deficit was 1.537 billion litas in the first quarter of this year versus 873 million litas in the same period in 1996.

- All Lithuanian television stations boycoted a news conference given by Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas at Vilnius airport Tuesday to protest against strict security measures imposed by the airport's administration.

- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas continues to top public opinion polls, according to the results of the most recent survey published by Baltic Surveys. He was followed by former prosecutor general Arturas Paulauskas and U.S. environmental bureaucrat Valdas Adamkus. Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius was ranked sixth followed by the chairman of parliament, Vytautas Landsbergis.
- The parliaments of Lithuania and Poland are expected to decide on an interparliamentary assembley on June 10-12.

- The chairman of parliament, Vytautas Landsbergis, voiced concern about the central bank's supervision policies. He also praised the work of former Bank of Lithuania governor Romualdas Visokavichius. The newspaper says Landsbergis' comments may be the opening shots in a battle to oust current central bank chief Reinoldijus Sharkinas.
- The computer technologies closed share company Alna sold a $2 million share issue to Hansa Investments.
- Estonia's Hansapank said it was eyeing Lithuania's market this year.
